7 Days to Die - I'm just starting with the game

Monster waves rotate on a fifty or so day basis. So after the 7th night horde on day fifty whatever with all the nasty zombies, it will revert to the first 7 day wave the following week and then ramp up again.

As for building, try digging underground to set up a temporary base while building your big one. The zombies aren't too good at digging down. Personally I prefer to dig a long tunnel into a mountain and set up base in there and use the long corridor as target practice. You can set up a basic airlock system with a couple of vault doors and some iron bars you can shoot through so you're always protected but still able to fire out.

And make sure you're aware of the heat map mechanic. It's a bit complicated for a text post so check the wiki.

Thanks for the advice and information about the rotation. I had heard of the heat map but just assumed it was the things that run on fire and a fading trail you left I will look it up for more details.

Here's a game I've been forced to take a break from. God damn real life and all... I've been thru 3 maps, the first two were write offs but the third I really get it. Probably 50 hours on first two maps, 100+ on my third go at it. The game is 60% hard work, 20 perseverance, 20 luck. All worth the effort. Read the wiki on heat mapping, its probably the only real "hidden" mechanic that coming to understand will save you headaches upon headaches when roaming hoards, or more specifically screamers wander your way.

To make life easier, perhaps make a 9x9 pad of spikes where below the spikes are your primary cooking stations (campfires and forges). Cookers tend to bring your heat map up pretty thick especially after a several days of use. These are what screamers are attracted to and always end up wandering towards. Cookers underground blanketed with spikes is easymode. This will probably make more sence if I weren't [6] and on mobile.

Oh, also, 0,0 coordinates on the map is almost always "hubcity" in random gen. Go find it, and hole up near it. But do not make a base in/around city limits until you've experienced Cops and Feral zombies en masse.

Bookstores are your friend. The sooner you can learn recipes such as the weapons (to assemble/repair on your own) and first aid kit. Arguably a bad idea to lean recipes you've already learned -- they increase your skill but don't increase your progress to next level (I've never test this, anyone please correct me). Just break them down for paper, you can always make shotgun shells or tvt with paper.

I think I'm done for now, I miss 7D2D. Hope my rambling makes sense, haven't gone back to correct any of it.

And don't let the game beat you down. Its designed to be a challenge, not easy. When you get a grip on the way it plays you'll then manage to destroy zombies and create master defensible bases on fresh new games.
